chunks.title: Shreya Singhal v. Union of India, (2015) 5 SCC 1
chunks.content:
### Shreya Singhal v. Union of India, (2015) 5 SCC 1
**Bench & Court:** Supreme Court of India (R.F. Nariman, J.)
**Core Holding:** Struck down Section 66A of the IT Act as unconstitutional for violating freedom of speech under Article 19(1)(a). Clarified Section 79 intermediary safe harbour: an intermediary must take down unlawful content only upon receiving actual knowledge via a court order or authorized government notification.

chunks.title: Anvar P.V. v. P.K. Basheer, (2014) 10 SCC 473
chunks.content:
### Anvar P.V. v. P.K. Basheer, (2014) 10 SCC 473
**Bench & Court:** Supreme Court of India (Kurian Joseph, J.)
**Core Holding:** Held that electronic records are inadmissible as secondary evidence unless accompanied by the mandatory statutory certificate. Oral evidence cannot substitute the certificate.

chunks.title: Arjun Panditrao Khotkar v. Kailash Kushanrao Gorantyal, (2020) 7 SCC 1
chunks.content:
### Arjun Panditrao Khotkar v. Kailash Kushanrao Gorantyal, (2020) 7 SCC 1
**Bench & Court:** Supreme Court of India (R.F. Nariman, J.)
**Core Holding:** Confirmed that producing a certificate is mandatory when secondary electronic evidence is tendered, but clarified that trial courts may direct production of the certificate where an official or entity refuses to furnish it.

chunks.title: Electronic Seizure & Hash Integrity Protocol
chunks.content:
### Electronic Seizure & Hash Integrity Protocol
1. **Digital Evidence Extraction:** Devices seized must be placed in Faraday bags, with SHA-256 or MD5 hash values generated immediately at the scene to prove no post-seizure tampering.
2. **Intermediary Notice Compliance:** Notice under Rule 3 of the IT (Intermediary Guidelines) Rules requires 36-hour takedown response window upon receipt of valid judicial order.

chunks.title: Information Technology Act, 2000 (IT Act)
chunks.content:
### Information Technology Act, 2000 (IT Act)
- **Section 43:** Penalty for damage to computer systems, unauthorized downloading, copying, virus injection, or denial of access.
- **Section 66:** Computer-related offences committed dishonestly or fraudulently punishable with imprisonment up to 3 years or fine up to ₹5 lakh.
- **Section 66C & 66D:** Identity theft using passwords/electronic signatures, and cheating by personation using computer resource.
- **Section 66E & 67:** Violation of bodily privacy and publishing or transmitting obscene material in electronic form.
- **Section 69A:** Power of Central Government to issue blocking directions for public access to computer information in the interest of sovereignty and public order.
- **Section 79 (Safe Harbour):** Intermediary liability exemption where the intermediary does not initiate transmission, select receiver, or modify content, subject to due diligence.

chunks.title: Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 Section 61 & 63 — Electronic Evidence
chunks.content:
### Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 Section 61 & 63 — Electronic Evidence
Mandatory electronic certificate verifying the system was operating properly, identifying the hash value, and establishing continuous chain of custody.
